issues.title: Make it clear who has authority for the final check
issues.author: rgwilton
issues.body:
IANA/RFC Editor runs the tools to check that the version of the doc to be published has the expected version.

If the tools report that it should be a major version but the approved version was a minor change, then as part of the AUTH48 process then the authors/ADs MUST sign off on releasing as a major version change.  YANG Doctors may be consulted if necessary to ensure that the right version is selected.

comments.author: rgwilton
comments.body:
From the meeting today:
 
We’ll have RFC editor and/or IANA folks run pyang with --check-update-semver.  If the suggested SemVer doesn’t match the one in the draft, then punt back to the AD to sort it out.  (I likely don’t have this quite correct, but it was something along those lines).
 
We’ll stick with pyang suggesting a minor bump when there are purely “questionable” changes (description, must, when, pattern). Maybe a note for Shepard’s checklist that all warnings have to have been chased down with authors?
 
Proposal for the IANA SemVer Guidelines doc: get it to a “usable draft”, and then let IANA actually use it for a few months (on at least a handful of actual updated YANG modules) before we bring it to WG LC.

issues.title: Should this document be informational or a BCP?
issues.author: rgwilton
issues.body: My uber level comment is, is this an Informational document? Owing to the extensive use of BCP 14 words, and if this language is intended to be binding, this document sounds more like a BCP than Informational. If that is not the intended, and you want to keep this informational, explicitly state that normative language in this draft is non-normative, i.e., clarify that the requirements are meant to be strong but not binding, and softening some of the MUST and SHOULD in the draft.

comments.author: rgwilton
comments.body: Yes, I think that this document should only be informational giving guidance.  I think that there are already existing documents that specify various requirements on IANA, and this documents is deliberately not trying to update or replace those.  The original goal here, was IANA asking for a more permanent reference of what steps are expected to process YANG files written in a way that could act as a reference and be shared with future team members, if required.  This document could be made into a BCP,  but given that the audience is small, then I'm not sure that is really required or helpful.

issues.title: Should the document use 2119 language?
issues.author: rgwilton
issues.body:
Document has Informational status, but uses the RFC2119 keywords "SHOULD NOT",
"SHOULD", "MUST NOT", "MUST", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MUST NOT", "SHOULD NOT", and
"RECOMMENDED". Check if this is really necessary?

comments.author: rgwilton
comments.body: I think that we want to careful not to get wrapped around the axel for using RFC 2119 language.  I.e., I think that it would be a bad idea to specify that RFC 2119 language has a different meaning in this doc because that would just end up being confusing.  Potentially the easiest fix is to just change to use lowercase statements rather RFC 2119 statements.   What do you think?

issues.title: Should this document change the process for when IANA publishes YANG modules from RFCs?
issues.author: rgwilton
issues.body:
Section 5.2.5, paragraph 0
>    IANA SHOULD delay publishing a normative YANG module to the IANA YANG
>    Parameters registry until the RFC Editor has completed editing the
>    module.  This coordination ensures that:

This is not the current practice: IANA typically acts upon IESG approval. 
This change needs explicit buy-in from IANA and should be clearly 
described as a process change, not just as guidance.

comments.author: rgwilton
comments.body: Regarding the timing of when YANG modules are published by IANA.  Yes, I agree that this is a deliberate process change.  Basically, I think that IETF/IANA should delay publishing the YANG module until any markups (e.g., from the RFC Editor) to the YANG module have been complete and the final version of the module (with the final version label) is ready, otherwise IANA will end up publishing a pre-release version.  I doubt that the existing process of when to publish is specified anywhere, and I'm not sure that we want this document to be defining the process.  Hence, that I propose is that it would be better for IANA + RFC Editor + IESG to agree on whether the process should change and then we can ensure it is documented correctly (informationally rather than normatively) in this document

pulls.body:
* update reference
* Added terminology from 9907 for consistency.
* make sure the guidance applies to normative modules (per 9907 terminology) not any random/example modules in an RFC.

and fixing nits.

Having frozen requirements (MUST) for pyang, etc. may not be appropriate in an RFC.

There is some guidance that is duplicate existing ones (e.g., RFC editor to make only editorial change, IANA to update a module, etc.). Better to refer to existing practice to avoid that we define new process, but simply leveraging existing.
